reflection.assumptions: Experiences of the pandemic may be shaped by health system preparedness, governance decisions, resource allocation, public health policies, and lessons carried forward from previous outbreaks such as Ebola. However, I recognize that my understanding of these experiences may not fully encompass the emotional realities and day-to-day experiences of patients and frontline workers during a crisis. I must also consider how individual perceptions and localized responses can influence broader health system dynamics.
reflection.further_consideration: How do the emotional experiences of patients and healthcare workers shape their perceptions of the healthcare system during a pandemic? How might these emotional experiences differ between various demographic groups, and what implications does this have for policy development and implementation? Additionally, how can governance structures better integrate these individual narratives into health policy design and implementation?

Initial Code: Decrease in patient inflow due to fear of COVID-19  
Clues: "But as soon as they sound the bell that there is a confirmed case in Sierra Leone, the patients in-flow dropped drastically. The patients were scared. They were afraid."  
Initial Code: Fear of healthcare settings leading to avoidance of medical care  
Clues: "They taught that as soon as they come to the hospital they will catch the virus. So they stayed back at home."  
Initial Code: Increased responsibilities for health workers during the pandemic  
Clues: "No. In fact as a matter of fact, it increased. It changed. It doubles up. Because I’ve to see the covid patients, and also do my normal clinical work."  
Initial Code: Implementation of triage system in response to COVID-19  
Clues: "But now it became compulsory as soon as you are at the hospital’s gate. You must wear your mask if not we won’t see you as health care workers."  
Initial Code: Change in surgical operations to prioritize emergencies  
Clues: "Only emergency patients will be operated on. All elective cases were put on hold."  
Initial Code: Training for health workers on new COVID-19 protocols  
Clues: "Trainings were held. That was a change. For example, for the use of the face masks, it was not compulsory in the hospital."  
Initial Code: Resource allocation challenges impacting service delivery  
Clues: "There were few masks, few of the gowns to be used, according to our operator."  
Initial Code: Return to normal operations after initial pandemic fears  
Clues: "But now we have revisited those laws again, so now all patients are given equal opportunities for surgical operations."  
Initial Code: Public perception of COVID-19 changing over time  
Clues: "As time passes by, the effect of afraid became drain by people. People start to believe, to assume now that the corona virus is with us."  
Initial Code: Increased patient load from referrals during COVID-19  
Clues: "Two district- [retracted] district and [retracted] district have outbreak of covid in their theaters. So they had their theaters shut down."  
Initial Code: Staff training on COVID-19 protocols  
Clues: "Yes there were trainings, especially in the line of covid-19. Were those staffs assigned to the covid-19 had their initial phase of training."  
Initial Code: Impact of staff training on workflow  
Clues: "It improved in the manner on how to touch patients. It also puts them on the gears of their tools and gears, that they should be using straight IPCs whenever handling a patient."  
Initial Code: General stress among staff due to COVID-19  
Clues: "Everyone was stressed with the covid-19. ... So that was why you will go all the way to attend the trainings."  
Initial Code: Fear of infection among healthcare workers  
Clues: "I was afraid. I was scared. Especially when there is no glove, I don’t touch patients. ... Everyone was afraid if that person doesn’t have masks and gloves to wear before touching a patient."  
Initial Code: Government provision of personal protective equipment  
Clues: "Later on the government then intervened and sent those IPCs- gloves, masks, the N95s."  
Initial Code: Decrease in patient flow during COVID-19  
Clues: "Yes, there have been changes as a result of the outbreak. ... When the outbreak started, there were minimal patients that we saw at the department."  
Initial Code: Changes in service delivery due to COVID-19  
Clues: "There was this hold-up on elective cases, handling only emergencies."  
Initial Code: Importance of adequate infection prevention control materials
